releases.name: 0.0.19: Commands read naturally with nothing after them
releases.body:
# v0.0.19

## Commands with nothing after them read as sentences

Hosts put the text after a command in place of `$ARGUMENTS` as written, so a command run with nothing after it left a
hole mid-sentence: `/estelle:resume` alone read "Call estelle_resume for ." and `code`, `monitor`, `review` and
`rooms` had the same gap.

Those five commands now say what to do in plain sentences and end with a labelled line that says what a blank means,
for example "Requested work (blank means the most recent): $ARGUMENTS". The change is in the shared commands and in
every host's generated copy: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, DeepSeek Harness, Grok Build, Kimi Code, OpenCode and Pi. A
new test runs every shared command with an empty argument and fails on the old wording. (#31)

## Docs

- The OpenCode and Pi install guides, the package READMEs, the README rows and the setup prompts install from npm
  (`opencode plugin @fatelabs/opencode-estelle -g`, `pi install npm:@fatelabs/pi-estelle`). (#30)
- The `estelle` skill's description names OpenCode and Pi among the hosts it is used from. (#30)

## Limits

- Nothing changed in the hooks, the MCP connection or the runtime beyond the version number.
- Pi still has no sub-agents, so Estelle's four agents are not available there.
- Rooms, explicit identity requests and mail sent to OpenCode and Pi sessions depend on the server change in
  Fate-Labs-CA/estelle#1992 (merged 2026-11-19). This release changes nothing on that path and was not re-run
  against it.

releases.name: 0.0.18: Estelle in OpenCode and Pi
releases.body:
# v0.0.18

## Estelle in OpenCode and Pi

Estelle now runs inside two more coding agents:

- **OpenCode** (`@fatelabs/opencode-estelle`, install with `opencode plugin @fatelabs/opencode-estelle -g`): the
  Estelle MCP server, the seven `/estelle:*` commands, the four agents as subagents, the skills and the instructions,
  with session identity, prompt recall, mail at the tool boundary and capture wired to OpenCode's own events.
- **Pi** (`@fatelabs/pi-estelle`, listed on pi.dev; install with `pi install npm:@fatelabs/pi-estelle`): the Estelle MCP
  server, `/estelle:*` commands, skills, session identity, recall, mail and capture through Pi's extension API.

Both were run live against a real model: the model called Estelle's tools and the hooks ran. See
docs/hosts/opencode.md and docs/hosts/pi.md for exactly what each host supports.

## Limits

- Pi has no sub-agents, so Estelle's four agents are not available there.
- The browser OAuth sign-in path and the billed cloud/handoff commands were not run live in either host.
- Rooms, explicit identity requests and mail sent to OpenCode and Pi sessions need the Estelle server from
  Fate-Labs-CA/estelle#1992.

releases.name: 0.0.17: sessions know who they are on Estelle, and messages reach a running session
releases.body:
# v0.0.17

## Sessions know who they are on Estelle, and messages reach a running session

Every session now gets its Estelle id and session token at every start, including after a compaction, so a message it
sends is marked verified. A message from another of your own sessions can be acted on; a message from a teammate's
session, or from an unverified sender, is shown to you first and waits for your yes.

Messages and room entries now reach a session at its next tool call, not only when you type, at most once every ten
seconds per session and never from a subagent's tool call. The sender can read a receipt: delivered, acknowledged,
answered.

Needs the Estelle server from Fate-Labs-CA/estelle#1878 (live on api.fatelabs.ca). Restart or `/compact` a running
session to give it its identity.

## Limits

- There is still no push into a model mid-reply: a session that is thinking without calling tools, or idle, gets its
  mail at its next tool call or prompt.
- Delivery is at most once: mail is marked delivered when it is handed to the hook.

releases.name: 0.0.16: cloud and handoff run on the small model in Claude Code
releases.body:
# v0.0.16

## Cloud and handoff run on the small model in Claude Code

`/estelle:cloud` and `/estelle:handoff` run one command on your machine and show you its link. In Claude Code that step
now runs on Haiku instead of your session's main model, which re-read your whole conversation just to run it.

This changes only that step on your machine. The agent in the cloud box picks its own model on Estelle's side, which is
Sonnet for Claude unless you choose another.

Nothing else changes, and other editors are unchanged.

## Limits

- Not run against a real cloud machine for this release, because each run starts a billed box.
- Whether Claude Code keeps Haiku when the model starts the command itself, rather than you typing it, is unmeasured.

releases.name: 0.0.15: the write check warns and never stops an edit
releases.body:
# v0.0.15

## The write check warns and no longer stops anything

Estelle's hook no longer refuses a file edit, on any host. Your agent can write a key into a file and the edit goes through.

When an edit writes an exact key shape, Estelle names the file and the kind of key, and tells you to rotate it if it's real. It
never repeats the value. The kinds are Stripe, Estelle, GitHub, OpenAI-style and Anthropic keys, Slack tokens, JWTs, private keys
with a body, Postgres URL passwords, and AWS, Google and SendGrid keys.

## What used to stop an edit and now does not

- **Every exact key shape above.** It warns, and the key is in your file.
- **Anything else, with no warning at all:** a value under a name such as `password = "..."` or `session_token = "..."`, an env file
  line, a long opaque value, a password in any URL other than a Postgres one, and a literal bearer header.

## What is unchanged

- Transcripts and session capture are still redacted the same way.
- `/estelle handoff` still leaves flagged files behind rather than pushing them, and still refuses a flagged unpushed commit. That
  scan is separate from this hook.
- Anything server-side that scans pull request content.

## Where you see the warning

| Host | Where |
|---|---|
| Claude Code, Codex | A system message for you, and context for the agent |
| Cursor | A user message and an agent message, with the edit allowed |
| Grok | Context for the agent |
| DeepSeek Harness | The harness log, and a message to the agent |
| Kimi | Hook stderr only: Kimi takes no context at this event, so you may not see it |

Every host also gets the warning on the hook's stderr.

## On Codex, approve the hooks again

This release changes the plugin's files, so Codex asks again: run `/hooks` and press `t`, or choose **Trust all and continue**.

## Limits

- Tested through each host's hook entry point with its own event shape, not inside the real host applications, so whether each
  one displays the words as described above has not been seen on screen.
- An unusual key that matches no listed shape gets no warning.
- A shell command that writes a file is still not looked at.
